change: Noted, no query changed: in OpenAlex a quoted phrase is matched on unstemmed text (title_and_abstract.search.exact), a bare word on stemmed text (title_and_abstract.search). A phrase without a trailing * therefore does not match its plural or other inflection

reason: dblp.org and its mirrors serve a browser bot-check page to programs (all 30 API requests failed on 29 Sep), and the search API cannot express the short forms: it drops quotes, turns every word into a prefix term and lets | join only adjacent single words, so the 15 answers Tagir fetched by hand on 30 Sep were all empty (evidence: data/raw/manual_exports/dblp/search_api_answers_by_hand_20260930.txt). The SPARQL route is DBLP's intended programmatic access and gives exact Boolean control; substring matching is slightly wider than word matching, which favours recall

change: IEEE retrieved through the IEEE Xplore Metadata API (personal key, 200 calls/day). The API accepts at most two wildcard words per request, so a form with more is sent as an exactly equivalent set of requests obtained by distributing OR over AND (union of parts = original set; no term added or removed); the threshold is applied to the sum of part counts (an upper bound) before retrieval and to the union after. Ordering by IEEE article number (the API offers no date sort); ordering has no role in inclusion. B4-Q27 has three AND groups with wildcards, so two of its parts cannot meet the limit and are reported
original_rule_or_query: Protocol section 4/5: IEEE Xplore form with bare * truncation; retrieval by API or export is an implementation choice
